extractor.note: Read every paragraph carrying transcend- (outside transcendental) or immanen-, in file order. No stratum is set: the record does not tie §§19-25 to the Prague lecture cycle.

coverage_note: Term-led pass over the whole file (lines 1-559): every paragraph containing the transcendence family, including bare transcendent and immanent, was read; paragraphs without such a word were not read.

units.claim: The Meditations substituted the psychic I for the ego and psychological immanence for egological immanence, with historical effect to the present.
units.quote: The Meditations worked themselves out in the fateful form of a substitution of the ego's own psychic I for the ego, psychological immanence for egological immanence

units.claim: Descartes' founding of philosophy from the ego is an epistemology of how the ego brings about objective cognition, which for him means cognition transcending the ego metaphysically.
units.quote: a theory of how the ego in the intentionality of its reason brings about objective cognition, which for Descartes means: cognition transcending the ego metaphysically

units.claim: Rationalism held that the method more geometrico can cognize the world thought of as a transcendent in-itself, and English empiricism reacted against this reach into a transcendent.
units.quote: Against this conviction — against such a reach of the new science into a "transcendent" — reacts English empiricism, though itself also strongly determined by Descartes.

units.claim: Cartesian presuppositionlessness demanded subjectively directed considerations, the return to the cognizing I in its immanence.
units.quote: The Cartesian radicalism of presuppositionlessness demanded subjectively directed considerations, the return to the cognizing I in its immanence.

units.claim: For Kant the natural-scientific world is a formation of the intellect, with the proviso that sensory material stems from a transcendent affection by things in themselves.
units.quote: only with the proviso that the material of sensory data stems from a transcendent affection by "things in themselves" that are in principle inaccessible to (objective-scientific) cognition

absences.expected_because: Dualism is treated here as the ground of the problems of reason, and §21 places rationalism's claim on a transcendent in-itself within the same development.
